trust_decision.summary: Whether the user connecting on the socket.io handshake owns the session whose client-supplied sessionId is being restored: restore_existing_session refuses the restore unless session.user.identifier matches the freshly authenticated user's identifier, with the both-None case allowed so unauthenticated deployments keep working.

landing_point.why: The advisory is a websocket session hijack, and restore_existing_session is the only place a client-supplied sessionId from the connect payload is turned back into a live session bound to a new socket (session.restore at socket.py:44).

fix_sites.module_kind: socket event handler helper (new function in backend/chainlit/socket.py)

fix_sites.entry_point: restore_existing_session, called only from the connect handler at socket.py:152-154
socket.io connect event, auth.sessionId restore branch

O3_reason_to_dismiss: WebsocketSession.restore() is an internal primitive with no other caller at the pinned commit, and the REST/feedback endpoints that reuse a sessionId are 'not the websocket restore path the advisory names', so neither is treated as covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unauthenticated deployments: require_login() is false, so connect passes user=None on every handshake; a session with session.user=None must still restore, otherwise every reconnect in an open deployment is refused and the pinned success test (which calls restore_existing_session with no user) breaks.

O6_input_shapes: unauthenticated connect (user=None) against an unauthenticated session (session.user=None) - must still restore
authenticated connect against a session created without a user (session.user=None, user set) - must refuse
authenticated connect against a session owned by the same identifier (User vs PersistedUser) - must restore
authenticated connect against a session owned by a different identifier - must refuse
restore of an unknown sessionId (get_by_id returns None) - unchanged fall-through to session creation

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PUT /feedback looks up the live session by the client-supplied sessionId (UpdateFeedbackRequest.sessionId) and runs config.code.on_feedback inside init_ws_context(session) with no comparison of session.user against current_user, while the six sibling sessionId routes all compare identifiers
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a REST feedback endpoint that never rebinds a socket, the lookup only runs when the app defines on_feedback and a data layer exists, and failures there are swallowed by the surrounding try/except - so it reads as 'not the restore path'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module from the landing point (server.py vs socket.py), ~850 lines away; same package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A REST endpoint that takes a client-supplied sessionId and drives the session (stop the running task, re-send a step, clear the session) via init_ws_context(get_by_id(sessionId)) with no ownership comparison.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Seven endpoints already follow exactly this shape (server.py:1071, 1107, 1257, 1313, 1465, 1510, 1644) and the react client posts sessionId on every one of them (libs/react-client/src/api/index.tsx:213, 302, 307, 313, 361), so an eighth endpoint that forgets the guard is the natural copy-paste slip.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second caller of WebsocketSession.restore() from a non-websocket bridge (e.g. a copilot/teams/slack adapter adopting a web session id) that rebinds the socket without any user context.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix guards the wrapper restore_existing_session, not the primitive; the primitive takes only a socket id, so it silently re-opens the sink for any new transport - and the repo already ships slack/teams/discord adapters that build sessions themselves (backend/chainlit/slack/app.py:311-313, backend/chainlit/teams/app.py:252-255).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'connection_successful'/'restore' socket event that accepts a sessionId in its payload and re-binds the session, in addition to the connect handshake.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The client already sends sessionId in the handshake auth map (libs/react-client/src/useChatSession.ts:122-133) and emits connection_successful right after (useChatSession.ts:142-145); a re-bind-on-event variant is a plausible refactor that would bypass the connect-time check.

O9_family: CWE-862 missing authorization / broken access control (cross-user session takeover)

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build, uv for the backend env (.github/actions/uv-python-install), pytest with asyncio_mode=auto and testpaths=backend/tests; the CI test job also runs pnpm run buildUi first
O10_build.project_tests: backend/tests/test_socket.py::TestRestoreExistingSession (test_restore_existing_session_success and test_restore_existing_session_not_found at the pinned commit; test_restore_existing_session_with_none_session_id at test_socket.py:409) plus the mocked-session route tests in backend/tests/test_server.py:241-300 (test_get_file_*) that exercise the same sessionId ownership comparison over HTTP

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add 'if not session.user or not user or session.user.identifier != user.identifier: raise ConnectionRefusedError' inside restore_existing_session (or immediately after the restore call in connect) and stop there; that refuses every reconnect in an unauthenticated deployment, the both-None case the pinned success test encodes.

out_of_scope_notes: POST /set-session-cookie (backend/chainlit/server.py:764-780) accepts an arbitrary session_id from an unauthenticated body and writes it into the X-Chainlit-Session-id cookie; it is the sticky-session helper, not the restore sink, so it was only noted.
